note: Live pages checked on 2026-07-15. Entries marked 'verificationFailed' could not be reached via WebFetch during research and must be re-verified before commit. All other entries are based on confirmed live deep URLs.

candidates.name: Quran.com
candidates.use: Tier-A primary. Canonical reader/tafsir/translations for any verse-level question. Multiple English translations including Saheeh International, Yusuf Ali, Pickthall, Mustafa Khattab.
candidates.limitations: Translation accuracy is reader's responsibility; Quran.com translations are not scholarly rulings. App does not equal tafsir authority. Always pair with a tafsir source for depth.

candidates.name: Sunnah.com
candidates.use: Tier-A primary hadith. Grades available per narration. Use English/Arabic display.
candidates.limitations: Grading shown is Sunnah.com's aggregation; some narrations need scholarly corroboration. Cross-check with Darussalam or Dorar metadata when chain is non-Bukhari.

candidates.name: Muwatta (Companion Site)
candidates.use: Tier-A primary Maliki hadith corpus (Imam Malik). Kept for completeness.
candidates.limitations: Companion site; if dormant may not be a strong surface. Verify liveness before committing deeper.

candidates.name: Altafsir.com — Royal Aal al-Bayt Institute
candidates.organization: Royal Aal al-Bayt Institute for Islamic Thought
candidates.use: Recommended Tier-A primary alongside Quran.com, Sunnah.com. Best-in-class tafsir aggregator (150+ tafsir texts in original Arabic). Endorsed by Al-Azhar and Columbia University references. Use for any tafsir-depth question.
candidates.limitations: Site has mixed encoding/legacy URLs (some pages use older Latin-1). The Tafasir.asp path is filter-driven and stable.

candidates.name: Egypt's Dar al-Ifta
candidates.use: Egyptian government fatwa institution. Six-language coverage. Cite for cross-madhhab reference in Egypt and Arab-diaspora-relevant answers. Pair with istiftas panel where relevant.
candidates.limitations: Some fatwas bear al-Azhar / Egyptian government perspective rather than independent ijtihad. Path patterns were confirmed live; verify `/en/fatwa/details/{id}` digests survive redirects.

candidates.name: Jordan General Iftaa Department
candidates.use: Jordanian official fatwa body, Hanafi legacy. Citable English fatwas currently slim — favor Arabic base. Pair with Dar al-Ifta for comparative opinions.
candidates.limitations: English fatwa path was confirmed on 2026-07-15; deep link has a known temporary outage banner. Path /en-fatwas/ numeric IDs are the citable surfaces.

candidates.name: Mufti of the Federal Territory
candidates.use: Pejabat Mufti WP — Malaysian fatwa council for Federal Territories. Path prefix `/en/artikel/...`. Robust Shafi'i lead with cross-madhhab angles. Recent topics include women in iddah, credit-card, EV charging, savings, zakat. Strong for finance + tech-fiqh.
candidates.limitations: JMWP covers Federal Territories only — for national-level Malaysian fatwas consider JaPPIM (Pusat Penterjemahan Mufti). Shafi'i bias; cite alongside Dar al-Ifta for cross-position.

candidates.name: AboutIslam — Ask the Scholar
candidates.use: About Islam's scholar sessions. Live dialogue mediated with named scholars (Dr. Mohammad S. Alrahawan visible on archive). Good for English diaspora-fatwa questions.
candidates.limitations: Live session format means transcripts vary in quality. Older transcripts are clearly dated; cite specific posts not the live landing page.

candidates.name: AboutIslam — Ask the Counselor
candidates.use: Counselor sessions — marriage/divorce, grief, mental-health emotional support. Counseling role, not fatwa role.
candidates.limitations: Counseling advice is not fatwa; in the citation always tag it as counseling.

candidates.name: Productive Muslim
candidates.use: Founded by Mohammed Faris, an AlMaghrib-trained UK-based productivity expert with strong Muslim professional audience (50,000+ newsletter). Citable for productivity, habits, AI-era work advice, faith-based career planning. Use `guidance` not `fatwa`.
candidates.limitations: Single-founder brand — opinion-led. Articles are good for practical guidance but never substitute for fatwa. AI era discussion is opinion, not a religious ruling.

candidates.name: IslamQA (al-Munajjid)
candidates.use: Sheikh Muhammad Saleh al-Munajjid Hanbali-leaning Saudi-fatwa archive. Translated into 15+ languages. Cite for any fatwa that surfaces a Hanbali/Salafi perspective.
candidates.limitations: Bias toward Munajjid/Salafi current. Always present along with one cross-madhhab fatwa for balance.

candidates.name: IslamWeb Fatwas
candidates.organization: Qatar Ministry of Awqaf & Islamic Affairs (IslamWeb.net)
candidates.use: Qatar's official Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs hosts this multilingual fatwa library. Cross-madhhab on most rulings; Salafi-leaning on edge cases. Cite as a Gulf-government-supported fatwa.
candidates.limitations: Editorial committee is multi-madhhab but selections lean toward the Saudi Salafi mainstream; pair with Egypt or Jordan for cross-check.

candidates.name: SeekersGuidance Answers
candidates.use: Toronto-based global seminary. Named-scholar fatwas (Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, Shaykh Irshaad Sedick, Mawlana Ilyas Patel). Cross-madhhab — every answer explicitly states the madhhab.
candidates.limitations: Less reach outside Hanafi-Shafi'i-Maliki English-speaking diaspora; cite together with at least one Saudi/Egyptian fatwa for balance.

candidates.name: IslamQA.org Multi-madhhab
candidates.use: Multi-madhhab split mirror of IslamQA-derivatives. Use to surface school-specific positions on the same question without rebuilding the answer from scratch.
candidates.limitations: Older mirror; verify stability of numeric ID paths before relying on it as a primary multi-madhhab source.

candidates.name: AMJA — Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America
candidates.organization: Assembly of Muslim Jurists of America
candidates.use: Major US-anchored multi-madhhab resident fatwa committee (~120 scholars). Cited as authoritative on US-context Islamic finance, family, medical, education, and minority-religious-life. Use `fatwa` role.
candidates.limitations: Fatwa Bank page is browseable; deep paths require search. Some short answer pages exist; treat direct-deeper paths as citable only after verifying they look like a fatwa-detail page.

candidates.name: IIFA — International Islamic Fiqh Academy
candidates.use: OIC-affiliated international Islamic fiqh academy (founded 1981). Official ijtihad decisions of OIC member-state scholars. Decisions cover: insect consumption (267/2025), genetically modified animal-origin foods (266/2025), cultured meat (265/2025), prem-infant milk kinship (264/2025), stunning before slaughter (263/2025), Shari'ah governance in Islamic financial institutions (262/2025). Use this for modern fiqh decisions that resolve worldwide queries.
candidates.limitations: Bilingualism is Arabic-primary; English translations lag. Decisions are majority resolutions, not always unanimous. Cite this in answer-model context that the answer carries the legitimacy of OIC consensus where present.

candidates.name: Office of Grand Ayatollah Sistani
candidates.organization: Office of His Eminence al-Sayyid Ali al-Husseini al-Sistani
candidates.use: Most-cited Shia marja' for global Twelver diaspora. Topic catalog under `/english/qa/{5-digit-id}/` (e.g. 01167 = Burial of the Dead, 01208 = Hijab, 01250 = Marriage, 01358 = Zakat, 01234 = Khums). Use fatwa role, madhhab = shia.
candidates.limitations: Path validation must be re-run before commit; the `/english/book/{title}/{id}/` pattern is independent and a separate lookup. Some pages may 404 if consolidated. Topics like "Migration to non-Muslim Countries" (01248) — exactly the minority-life lane.

candidates.name: Al-Khoei Foundation
candidates.use: Imam al-Khoei marja library, Ja'fari school with significant London presence. Useful when Sistani is unfamiliar or user follows Abu al-Qasim al-Khui marja' line.
candidates.limitations: Site is primarily Arabic. English path equivalents exist but editorial moderation is slower. Verify before commit.

candidates.name: Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research
candidates.use: Yaqeen Institute's research papers cover AI ethics, mental health, marriage/gender, parenting, social justice, prayer's psychology. Highest-quality contemporary English-language scholarship in the Muslim institutional world. Use `guidance`, not `fatwa`.
candidates.limitations: Guidance role. For rulings, defer to a fatwa source. Yaqeen explicitly does not issue fatwa.

candidates.name: Khalil Center — Psychological & Spiritual Wellness
candidates.use: Premier Islamic psychotherapy institution (founded 2004). Publishes TIIP (Traditional Islamically Integrated Psychotherapy) and case-study articles that connect spiritual practice to clinical mental health practice. Citable for emotional, grief, anxiety, marriage, family, premarital coaching content.
candidates.limitations: Counseling articles are not clinical guidelines; never use as a substitute for medical/clinical advice. Cite only article pages, never the request-appointment / login paths.

candidates.name: Islamic Medical Association of North America
candidates.organization: Islamic Medical Association of North America (IMANA)
candidates.use: IMANA — established 1967 US-Muslim medical professional body. Maintains awareness articles on UV safety, men's health, world blood donor day, mental health awareness month, Ramadan dental, public health. Useful for English-language public health guidance tied to Muslim faith. Use `guidance`.
candidates.limitations: Articles are not medical advice. Never substitutes for clinical care. Articles prefixed by date or category are citable (e.g. `/2026/04/15/...`).

candidates.name: Islamic Relief Worldwide — Knowledge Base
candidates.organization: Islamic Relief Worldwide (UK registered, global operations)
candidates.use: Major UK-based Muslim humanitarian NGO with a sizeable knowledge base on zakat, sadaqah, riba, waqf, aqiqah, fidya, kaffarah, umrah rules, charity. Decades of charitable-context practice. Use `guidance`, not `fatwa`.
candidates.limitations: Not a fatwa body. For rulings on specific transactions defer to Mufti WP, Egypt Dar al-Ifta, AMJA, or AAOIFI.

candidates.name: CrescentRating — Muslim-Friendly Travel Intelligence
candidates.use: Industry body producing the Mastercard-CrescentRating Global Muslim Travel Index (GMTI). Citable for travel-related questions (halal-friendly destinations, prayer access at airports/hotels, etc.).
candidates.limitations: Industry/commercial body. Use for travel logistics, not fiqh rulings. Not a fatwa source.

candidates.name: IFANCA — Islamic Food and Nutrition Council of America
candidates.organization: Islamic Food and Nutrition Council of America
candidates.use: Technical halal authority since 1982. Citable for confirmation that a manufacturer/product has IFANCA halal certification and what the certification process entails. NOT a fatwa source — its role is technical (certification) and not religious (haram/halal ruling on a substance).
candidates.limitations: Industry body. Not a fatwa body. For ruling on a novel ingredient, defer to AAOIFI standard text, Mufti WP, or IIFA decisions.

candidates.name: Bayyinah Institute (Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan)
candidates.use: US-based Quranic Arabic institute led by Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan. Articles and event pages are citable educational content. Sister online platform bayyinah.tv hosts courses.
candidates.limitations: Not a fatwa body. Use as guidance for Quranic Arabic, tafsir-style articles, learning paths.

candidates.name: AlMaghrib Institute
candidates.use: AlMaghrib Institute — founded 2002 by Sheikh Muhammad Alshareef (rA). 21+ instructors, 300,000+ students, programs in `aqeedah, fiqh, tafsir, hadith, seerah, personal development, mental well-being`. Use for Islamic-learning outcomes, syllabus, mental-wellbeing curriculum.
candidates.limitations: Not a fatwa body. References to specific course content are citable; the homepage and program pages do not establish rulings.

candidates.name: Al-Huda International Welfare Foundation
candidates.use: Pakistan-based Quranic women's institute founded 1994 (Dr. Farhat Hashmi). Audio-based Tafseer al-Quran, Fahm al-Quran courses. Useful as Urdu-language deep education reference.
candidates.limitations: Mostly Urdu audio/text content. English limited. Verify audio paths before relying on them as citable.

candidates.name: Al-Mawrid — Foundation for Islamic Research & Education
candidates.use: Pakistan-based foundation. Use as a scholarly guidance source for English coverage when paired with audio lectures.
candidates.limitations: Homepage renders thin; article-paths must be verified before heavy reliance. Verify live paths in QA.

candidates.name: New Muslim Academy
candidates.use: Convert-focused resource center for newly-Muslim students. Citable for new-Muslim life basics.
candidates.limitations: Free-registration oriented; the actual substantive content is behind login for some pages. Public articles only.

candidates.name: muslim.or.id (YPIA Al-Atsari)
candidates.use: Indonesian-language YPIA (Al-Atsari) scholarly publishing house. Strong on ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth-grade discussions, AI ethics, riba, mental health (depression from Islamic angle), corruption. Useful as Indonesian-language cultural entry into Sunni scholarly discussion.
candidates.limitations: Indonesian Salafi-leaning editorial line; cross-madhhab citations needed for any ruling. The site uses Indonesian, not English; Arabic-script URLs sometimes used.

candidates.name: KonsultasiSyariah — Yufid Network
candidates.use: Indonesian-language scholar network by Yufid.TV — large Indonesian-language fiqh-tazkiyah-sirah archive. Sister site to bayyina.org and the Yufid media arm. Topical depth in Indonesian Islamic life questions.
candidates.limitations: Indonesian Salafi-leaning editorial line; some content is append-only. Path patterns must be checked for stability of numeric 5-digit IDs.
